**Section C: Reading Comprehension (10 marks).** Read the following passage on the history of warfare carefully and answer the questions based on it. The passage traces the evolution of weapons from hand-thrown stones, through catapults, bows and arrows, and swords, to guns, grenades, bombs and, ultimately, nuclear and chemical warheads and missiles.

1. How many types of weapons are mentioned in the passage? Name them. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 1. **About eight types of weapons are mentioned:** (1) hand-thrown stones, (2) the catapult, (3) the bow and arrow, (4) the sword, (5) the gun and bullet, (6) grenades, (7) bombs, and (8) missiles/nuclear and chemical warheads.

2. Which three factors, according to the passage, initially determined the amount of damage a weapon like the bow and arrow could cause? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 2. **The size of the bow, the elasticity/tension of its string, and the sharpness of the arrow** together determined how much damage the weapon could cause.

3. What is a catapult, and why was its impact limited? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 3. **A catapult, as described in the passage, was a primitively made weapon consisting of a tough rope with a heavy stone tied to one end.** Its impact was limited because, however strong the force behind it, it could only strike one target/person at a time.

6. Was the invention of the gun a revolution in warfare? Why? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 6. **Yes, it was a revolution**, because for the first time a single foot soldier could kill enemies from a distance with minimal physical effort — simply by pulling a trigger — and could inflict casualties on a scale far beyond what earlier hand-thrown or bladed weapons ever allowed.

7. Which weapons does the passage compare to toys today, and why? (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown: 7. **The earlier weapons — the stone, the catapult, the bow and arrow, and the sword — are compared to toys today**, because their destructive power appears negligible next to that of grenades, bombs, missiles and nuclear or chemical warheads.

8. In your opinion, which is the most dangerous weapon today? Do you agree with the author that this represents "development"? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 8. **The most dangerous weapons today are nuclear and chemical warheads/missiles**, capable of destroying entire cities within hours. Whether this amounts to true "development" is debatable: as a feat of engineering it is undeniably advanced, but genuine development should improve human wellbeing, whereas these weapons exist chiefly to cause mass destruction — a personal, argued answer is expected here, and both a supporting and an opposing view can be validly defended.

incertitudes: La question 8 appelle une opinion personnelle argumentée ; la réponse proposée présente la position la plus courante mais une réponse défendant le point de vue inverse, si elle est bien argumentée à partir du texte, reste valable.
